## What Is an Employer of Record in Seychelles


An Employer of Record (EOR) is a third-party company that becomes the legal employer on paper in a given country while you retain full control over the employee's day-to-day work. In Seychelles, that means the EOR signs the employment contract, runs payroll in Seychellois Rupees, and holds all statutory obligations under local law. You direct the work. The EOR handles the paperwork.


### How the Legal Employer Structure Works in Seychelles


Employment in Seychelles is primarily governed by the[Employment Act 1995](https://www.lawgratis.com/blog-detail/employment-law-in-seychelles) , the Labour Relations Act 2008, and related regulations covering contracts, wages, working hours, leave, termination, and disputes. Under an EOR model, the EOR's local entity signs compliant employment contracts, withholds taxes, and meets every statutory requirement under that framework. You keep full control: you set the role, manage performance, and direct the work. The EOR carries the legal employer risk.


### When Foreign Companies Use an EOR Instead of a Local Entity


Setting up a Seychelles business entity means registration fees, legal overhead, and ongoing compliance obligations before you've hired a single person. For companies testing the market or making an early hire, that's a real commitment. An EOR removes the need for a local entity entirely, letting you[hire globally without the complexity](https://www.bolto.com/employer-of-record) of entity setup, onboarding a Seychelles-based employee in days, not months.


## Employment Laws and Compliance Requirements in Seychelles


Seychelles employment law sits across several statutes, and getting the details wrong creates real liability. Here's what foreign employers are responsible for.


### Contracts and Probation


Written contracts are strongly recommended under Seychelles law, whether indefinite or fixed-term. Probationary periods may run up to six months under Section 70(b) of the Employment Act 1995, with shorter notice obligations on both sides during that window. (Seychelles Ministry of Employment, 2025)


### Social Security and Payroll Tax Obligations


Obligation Employer Rate Employee Rate Remittance Deadline


Seychelles Pension Fund (SPF) 5% (Seychelles Pension Fund, effective January 2023) 5% (Seychelles Pension Fund, effective January 2023) 21st of following month


Social Security Fund (SSF) ~15% ~3% 21st of following month


Pay As You Earn (PAYE) Income Tax (residents) Withheld (progressive 0-30%) (SRC, effective June 2018) Employee bears 21st of following month


PAYE Income Tax (expatriates) Withheld (progressive; minimum 15%, up to 30%) (SRC, effective June 2018) Employee bears 21st of following month


Non-Monetary Benefits Tax 15% on non-cash benefits (SRC, effective January 2023) N/A 21st of following month


*Rates are general figures based on*[published sources](https://www.playroll.com/payroll/seychelles) *and may be updated by the Seychelles Revenue Commission. Verify current rates with a qualified adviser before processing payroll.*


### Leave Entitlements


Female employees are generally entitled to 16 weeks of paid maternity leave, of which not less than 12 weeks shall be taken after the date of confinement (Seychelles Ministry of Employment, 2025, citing Regulation 16 of the Employment (Conditions of Employment) Regulations 1991 as amended in 2018); paternity leave is 2 days. Standard annual leave and public holiday entitlements also apply.


### Notice Periods and Severance


Notice scales with tenure. Employees with at least one year of continuous service are generally entitled to severance pay, with the standard calculation being one month's average wage per year of service, provided termination is not for serious misconduct.


*This is general information, not legal advice. Rules vary by situation and change over time, so consult a qualified employment lawyer for your specific circumstances.*

Direct entity establishment in Seychelles involves business registration, appointing a local director or registered agent, registering with the SRC for PAYE, and registering separately with the Seychelles Pension Fund (SPF) for social security contributions. Each step carries professional fees before you can legally pay a single employee. That fixed overhead applies whether you hire one person or ten.
